chapterTitle: FBISE Annual Exam Simulator 01 (Unit 9 & 10: Equilibrium, Acids, Bases & Salts)
subject: chemistry-10

questions.question: For the reversible reaction $N_2(g) + 3H_2(g) \rightleftharpoons 2NH_3(g)$, what is the unit of $K_c$?
At dynamic equilibrium in a closed system:

options.A: The forward and reverse reaction rates become equal
options.D: Color of the reaction mixture changes continuously

questions.explanation: Dynamic chemical equilibrium occurs when the forward and reverse reactions proceed at equal rates, keeping macroscopic properties constant.

questions.question: If $Q_c < K_c$, the net chemical reaction will proceed:

options.A: In the forward direction (left to right)
options.B: In the reverse direction (right to left)

questions.explanation: When the reaction quotient $Q_c$ is less than $K_c$, product concentration is lower than at equilibrium, driving the reaction forward.

questions.question: Which of the following compounds is a Lewis acid that acts as an electron pair acceptor?
questions.explanation: Boron trifluoride ($BF_3$) has an incomplete octet (6 valence electrons around boron) and acts as an electron-pair acceptor (Lewis acid).

questions.question: What is the conjugate acid of the sulphate ion ($SO_4^{2-}$)?
questions.explanation: A conjugate acid is formed when a base accepts one proton ($H^+$). When $SO_4^{2-}$ accepts $H^+$, it forms the hydrogen sulphate ion ($HSO_4^-$).

questions.question: What is the pH of a $1.0 \times 10^{-4}\text{ M } HCl$ solution at $25^\circ\text{C}$?
questions.explanation: $HCl$ completely dissociates to produce $[H^+] = 10^{-4}\text{ M}$. Therefore, $pH = -\log(10^{-4}) = 4$.

questions.question: What color does phenolphthalein indicator exhibit in a solution with a pH of 11?
questions.explanation: Phenolphthalein is colorless in acidic and neutral solutions ($pH < 8.3$) and turns vibrant pink in alkaline solutions ($pH > 8.3$).

questions.question: Which gas is evolved with vigorous effervescence when dilute nitric acid reacts with sodium bicarbonate ($NaHCO_3$)?
questions.explanation: Acids react with bicarbonates to produce salt, water, and liberate carbon dioxide gas ($NaHCO_3 + HNO_3 \to NaNO_3 + H_2O + CO_2\uparrow$).

questions.question: Which of the following salts is classified as an acidic salt?
questions.explanation: Sodium bisulphate ($NaHSO_4$) is an acidic salt because it still retains an ionizable, replaceable hydrogen ion from sulphuric acid.

questions.question: Potash alum ($K_2SO_4 \cdot Al_2(SO_4)_3 \cdot 24H_2O$) is an authentic example of a:
questions.explanation: Potash alum is an equimolar crystalline combination of two simple salts ($K_2SO_4$ and $Al_2(SO_4)_3$), classifying it as a double salt.

questions.question: The ionic product of water ($K_w$) at $25^\circ\text{C}$ is numerically equal to:
What is the unit of $K_c$ for the reaction $H_2(g) + I_2(g) \rightleftharpoons 2HI(g)$?
questions.explanation: Since total moles of reactants ($1+1=2$) equals total moles of products ($2$), $\Delta n = 0$ and $K_c$ has no units.
